chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Faḍālah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:

My father asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a person who lends his garment to someone whom he knows eats al-jirrī and drinks wine, then he returns it: may he perform salat (prayer) in it before washing it? He said: He should not perform salat (prayer) in it before washing it.

Thus, both of these reports are narrated by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, and in both of them the account concerns his father's question to Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام. It is not permissible, as you can see, for them to be contradictory such that he says at one time, 'Perform salat (prayer) in it,' and at another time says, 'Do not perform salat (prayer) in it,' unless his statement, 'Do not perform salat (prayer) in it,' is to be understood as indicating dislike rather than prohibition.

key_terms.الْجِرِّيَّ: a type of fish mentioned here as something eaten by the borrower
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislike or reprehensibility in a legal sense
key_terms.ثَوْبَهُ: his garment used here as clothing for salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَغْسِلَهُ: to wash the garment before use in salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) in a garment returned by someone who drinks wine and eats impure things before washing it?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on performing salat (prayer) in a garment that had been lent to someone known to consume impure or forbidden things and then returned. The apparent prohibition is reconciled by understanding it as karāhah rather than absolute prohibition, indicating a juristic treatment of impurity, caution, and prayer garments.
